record.title: Franke–Muthiah conjecture on two-dimensional convex embeddings
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a code. Its **minimal convex embedding dimension** is the least dimension in which it admits a convex realization, and its **minimal open convex embedding dimension** is the least dimension in which it admits an open convex realization. **Franke–Muthiah's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{C}$ is open convex and has minimal open convex embedding dimension $2$, then the minimal convex embedding dimension of $\mathcal{C}$ is $2$. This conjecture concerns the relation between open convex and convex realizations in dimension $2$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Neha Gupta and Suhith K N, “Neural Codes and Neural ring endomorphisms”, arXiv:2106.06565 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06565

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: The regular-orbit conjecture for cubic vertex-transitive graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a cubic vertex-transitive graph of order $n$ that is not isomorphic to $K_{3,3}$ or a split Praeger–Xu graph, and let $g\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$. A **regular orbit** of $g$ is an orbit whose size equals the order of $g$. **The regular-orbit conjecture.** At least

$$
\frac{2}{3}n
$$

vertices of $\Gamma$ lie on a regular orbit of $g$. The claim is motivated by a family of cubic vertex-transitive graphs in which two thirds of the vertices lie on regular orbits, and by the assertion that split Praeger–Xu graphs are the exceptional extreme case. Its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Primoz Potocnik, Micael Toledo and Gabriel Verret, “On orders of automorphisms of vertex-transitive graphs”, arXiv:2106.06750 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06750

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Kalai–Whiteley maximality conjecture for hyperconnectivity matroids
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}_d(n)$ be the generic hyperconnectivity matroid on the edges of the complete graph. Let $K_{d+2}$ be a complete graph on $d+2$ vertices and $K_{d+1,d+1}$ a complete bipartite graph with parts of size $d+1$.

**Kalai–Whiteley maximality conjecture.** The matroid $\mathcal{H}_d(n)$ is the freest matroid in which every $K_{d+2}$ and every $K_{d+1,d+1}$ are circuits.

This is known for $d=1$ and remains open for $d=2$; the source gives no resolution in higher dimensions. Partial results are attributed to Jackson and Tanigawa.

record.title: Hurwitz stability conjecture for the alternating-run polynomial
record.statement:
Let $r(x)=\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}$ and define $\mathscr{R}_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{2n-1}\mathscr{R}(n,k)x^k$ by

$$
(xD_x)^n(r(x))=\frac{\mathscr{R}_n(x)}{(1-x)^n(1+x)^{n-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
$$

The recurrence is

$$
\mathscr{R}_{n+1}(x)=(2nx+1)x\mathscr{R}_n(x)+x(1-x^2)D_x\mathscr{R}_n(x),
$$

with $\mathscr{R}_0(x)=1$ and $\mathscr{R}_1(x)=x$. **Hurwitz stability conjecture.** The polynomial $\mathscr{R}_n(x)$ is Hurwitz stable for $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The coefficients count dual Stirling permutations by alternating runs, and the polynomial is not real-rooted; the conjecture asserts the stronger half-plane location property instead. Its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Ming-Jian Ding and Bao-Xuan Zhu, “Stability of combinatorial polynomials and its applications”, arXiv:2106.12176 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: The Brill–Noether gonality conjecture for finite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected loopless multigraph, and let $g:= |E(G)| - |V(G)| + 1$ denote its cyclomatic number. **Brill–Noether gonality conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{dgon}(G) \leq \left\lfloor\frac{g + 3}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is the $r=1$ case of the Brill–Noether conjecture for finite graphs, an analogue of the corresponding result for algebraic curves. The paper focuses on this case; the supplied text does not establish its resolution.
record.source_name: Josse van Dobben de Bruyn, Harry Smit and Marieke van der Wegen, “Discrete and metric divisorial gonality can be different”, arXiv:2106.12568 (2021).

record.title: Characterization of divergence by order via non-cyclic subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $n$ be the fixed path-order parameter, and let $HL^k(G)$ denote the graph obtained after applying the $P_n$-line graph operator $k$ times. A connected subgraph $G'$ of $HL^k(G)$ contains a cycle $C_m$ when it has a subgraph isomorphic to $C_m$.

**Divergence characterization conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a sequence that diverges by order if and only if there exists a $k$ such that $HL^k(G)$ has a connected subgraph $G'$ where $G'$ has a subgraph isomorphic to $C_m$ ($m\geq n$) but $G'\not\cong C_m$.

The preceding theorem proves the sufficiency of the stated structural condition; the conjecture asserts that this condition is also necessary.
record.source_name: Alvaro Carbonero, “Towards a characterization of convergent sequences of P_n-line graphs”, arXiv:2107.03905 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03905

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: Unicyclic-components conjecture for minimally $n$-convergent graphs
record.statement:
Let $\lambda_n$ denote the class of minimally $n$-convergent graphs, and let the components of a graph be its connected components. A component is **unicyclic** when it contains exactly one cycle.

**Unicyclic-components conjecture.** If $G\in\lambda_n$, then $G$ has unicyclic components.

The conjecture concerns the structure of minimally $n$-convergent graphs and is presented as a proposed structural description that would facilitate further results about these graphs.
record.source_name: Alvaro Carbonero, “Towards a characterization of convergent sequences of P_n-line graphs”, arXiv:2107.03905 (2021).

record.title: Unique minimal convergent subgraph conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda_n$ denote the class of graphs whose $P_n$-line graph sequences converge, and let $\lambda_n$ denote the class of minimally $n$-convergent graphs. For graphs $G$ and $G'$, write $G'\subseteq G$ when $G'$ is a subgraph of $G$.

**Unique minimal subgraph conjecture.** If $G\in\Lambda_n$ and $G$ is not the disconnected union of two graphs in $\Lambda_n$, then there exists a unique graph $G'\in\lambda_n$ such that $G'\subseteq G$.

The conjecture is proposed as a further direction in the study of minimally $n$-convergent graphs; the preceding theorem gives a related preservation result for unicyclic components under an additional girth hypothesis.

record.title: Tong-Viet's regular character-graph conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $\Delta(G)$ be its character graph: its vertices are the primes dividing some irreducible character degree of $G$, with two distinct primes adjacent when their product divides such a degree. **Tong-Viet's conjecture.** If $\Delta(G)$ is $k$-regular for some integer $k\geqslant 2$, then $\Delta(G)$ is either a complete graph of order $k+1$ or a cocktail party graph of order $k+2$. The conjecture concerns the possible structure of regular character graphs; the paper studies regular character graphs whose eigenvalues are at least $-2$, while the supplied text records no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Mahdi Ebrahimi, Maryam Khatami and Zohreh Mirzaei, “Regular character-graphs whose eigenvalues are greater than or equal to -2”, arXiv:2107.05837 (2021).

record.title: Ryser's conjecture in the remaining 2-packing cases
record.statement:
Let $r\geq3$ be an integer. Consider an intersecting $r$-partite linear system, with transversal number $\tau$ and 2-packing number $\nu_2$.

**Ryser's conjecture in the remaining 2-packing cases.** Every such system satisfies

$$
\begin{cases}
\tau\leq r-1 & \text{if } \nu_2=r+1 \text{ and } r\geq3 \text{ is odd},\\
\tau\leq r-1 & \text{if } \nu_2=r \text{ and } r\geq4 \text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

These are the two cases left after the paper's preceding results on the 2-packing number. Proving both would establish the intersecting linear form of Ryser's conjecture, but the supplied text does not indicate that they have been resolved.
record.source_name: Adrián Vázquez Ávila, “A note on extremal intersecting linear Ryser systems”, arXiv:2108.01108 (2021).

record.title: Meagher–Razafimahatratra–Spiga conjecture on derangement graphs of even-degree groups
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an even integer that is not a power of $2$. A transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $n$ has derangement graph $\Gamma_G$.

**Meagher–Razafimahatratra–Spiga's conjecture.** There exists a transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $n$ such that $\Gamma_G$ is a complete multipartite graph with $n/2$ parts.

This conjecture concerns the existence of transitive permutation groups whose derangement graphs have a highly structured complete multipartite form. It was posed as the main motivation for the paper; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.

record.title: Abrishami's common Laplacian eigenvalues conjecture for equivalent cographs
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be equivalent cographs with reductions $R_G$ and $R_H$. Suppose the vertices of $R_G$ and $R_H$ are labeled by the twin numbers $t_i$ of the $k$ twin classes they represent. Here, a twin class is a class of vertices represented by one vertex in the reduction, and its type records the corresponding type in the cograph.

**Abrishami's conjecture.** $G$ and $H$ have at least

$$
k + \sum_{i\in I}(t_i-1)
$$

Laplacian eigenvalues in common, where $I$ is the set of indices of the twin classes whose types are identical in $G$ and $H$.

This conjecture concerns how much of the Laplacian spectrum is preserved between equivalent cographs. The supplied source attributes it to Tara Abrishami's master's thesis, but gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: J. Lazzarin, O. F. Márquez and F. C. Tura, “Laplacian eigenvalues of equivalent cographs”, arXiv:2108.04873 (2021).

record.title: Ding's tri-weight code conjecture for trinomial value-sets
record.statement:
Let $m\ge 5$ be an odd integer. Let $f$ be any trinomial specified in the paper, let $D(f)^*$ be its punctured value-set, and let $\mathcal{C}_{D(f)^*}$ denote the associated binary trace code. **Ding's tri-weight code conjecture.** The code $\mathcal{C}_{D(f)^*}$ is a $[2^{m-1},m,2^{m-2}-2^{(m-3)/2}]$-code with weight enumerator polynomial

$$
1+(2^{m-2}-2^{(m-3)/2})z^{2^{m-2}-2^{(m-3)/2}}+(2^{m-1}-1)z^{2^{m-2}}+(2^{m-2}+2^{(m-3)/2})z^{2^{m-2}+2^{(m-3)/2}}.
$$

Furthermore, the dual code of $\mathcal{C}_{D(f)^*}$ is a $[2^{m-1},2^{m-1}-m,3]$-code. The abstract says that the paper gives a partial resolution of this conjecture, while the displayed formulation records the full claimed parameters and weight distribution.
record.source_name: Omran Ahmadi and Masoud Shafaeiabr, “Difference sets and tri-weight linear codes from trinomials over binary fields”, arXiv:2108.10042 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10042

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: The lower-bound sharpness conjecture for $K_5^<$
record.statement:
Let $K_5^<$ be the $3$-graph on five vertices with eight edges whose two missing edges intersect in exactly two vertices. The supplied bounds are

$$
\frac{5}{9}\leq\pi(K_5^<),\quad \frac{1}{3}\leq\sigma(K_5^<),\quad \frac{1}{2}\leq\pi_2(K_5^<),\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{1}{2}\leq\pi_u(K_5^<).
$$

**The lower-bound sharpness conjecture for $K_5^<$.** All four lower bounds are sharp:

$$
\pi(K_5^<)=\frac{5}{9},\qquad \sigma(K_5^<)=\frac{1}{3},\qquad \pi_2(K_5^<)=\frac{1}{2},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \pi_u(K_5^<)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

The text gives flag-algebra upper bounds that are strictly above these lower bounds, so the conjecture remains open in the supplied material.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen and Bernard Lidický, “Hypergraph Turán Problems in _2-Norm”, arXiv:2108.10406 (2025).
record.references:

record.title: The slightly less bold conjecture on elementary entailment
record.statement: Let $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ be linear data, and let $\gamma$ be a partial matching map as in the paper. Write $\Phi\vdash'^k_\gamma\Psi$ for entailment using the additional elementary elimination rule, and $\Phi\vdash^{k'}_\gamma\Psi$ for entailment using only the original Cauchy–Schwarz rules. **Slightly less bold conjecture.** If $\Phi\vdash'^k_\gamma\Psi$, then there exists some $k'\geq0$ such that $\Phi\vdash^{k'}_\gamma\Psi$. This asks whether every entailment obtained from an elementary functional-equation argument can be simulated by repeated Cauchy–Schwarz applications; the source gives no resolution and notes possible difficulties with eliminating non-trivial subexpressions.
record.source_name: Freddie Manners, “True complexity and iterated Cauchy–Schwarz”, arXiv:2109.05731 (2021).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2021). “It is not too hard to find natural systems of linear forms where Conjecture applies but is open.”

record.title: Supersaturation conjecture for even-town families
record.statement:
For a set family $[?]$ and distinct sets $A,B\begin{pmatrix}\in\mathcal{A}\end{pmatrix}$, let $peratorname{op}[?]([?])$ denote the number of pairs whose intersection has odd size. Here $2^{[n]}$ is the power set of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and $[?]$ consists only of even-sized subsets. 

**Supersaturation conjecture.** Let $n\geq 1$ and fix $3\leq s\leq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}-2^{\lfloor n/4\rfloor}$. If $[?]\subset 2^{[n]}$ consists of even-sized subsets with $|[?]|\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}+s$, then

$$
\operatorname{op}(\mathcal{A})\geq s\cdot 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1}.
$$

The statement extends the paper's proved cases $s=1,2$ and asserts that the described even-town construction remains extremal throughout the indicated range; its status is presented as conjectural in the source.
record.source_name: Jason O'Neill, “A short note on supersaturation for oddtown and eventown”, arXiv:2109.09925 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09925

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Jaeger–Zhang conjecture for signed planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{P}^*_{4p+1}$ denote the class of signed planar graphs with the indicated girth condition. **Jaeger–Zhang conjecture.**

$$
\chi_c(\mathcal{P}^*_{4p+1})\leq \frac{2p+1}{p}.
$$

This conjecture gives an upper bound for the circular chromatic numbers of the corresponding classes of signed planar graphs; the paper presents it as a notable conjecture, while the surrounding discussion indicates that determining the exact values and closing the known bounds remain open problems.
record.source_name: Reza Naserasr and Zhouningxin Wang, “Signed bipartite circular cliques and a bipartite analogue of Grötzsch's theorem”, arXiv:2109.12618 (2021).

record.title: Dual equivalence-relation conjecture for q-matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a $q$-matroid, and let $M^*$ denote its dual. The relation of Definition is defined on $M$ and $M^*$.

**Dual equivalence-relation conjecture.** The relation of Definition is an equivalence relation in at least one of $M$ and $M^*$.

The conjecture is motivated by examples in which the relation is an equivalence relation for some $q$-matroids but does not behave as desired for direct-sum decompositions or under duality. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: NP-completeness conjecture for APUD(k,m) recognition
record.statement:
For integers $k$ and $m$, let $\mathrm{APUD}(k,m)$ denote the graph class consisting of intersection graphs of disks whose centers lie on $k$ parallel lines, with the relevant representation restricted by parameter $m$.

**APUD recognition conjecture.** Recognition of $\mathrm{APUD}(k,m)$ is NP-complete.

The paper proves NP-completeness for the special case $m=0$ and asks whether the technique can establish NP membership for general $m$. Thus the general recognition claim remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Onur Çağırıcı, “Computational Aspects of Problems on Visibility and Disk Graph Representations”, arXiv:2111.00609 (2021).

record.title: Red's one-tile advantage conjecture for Infinite Hex
record.statement:
Consider Infinite Hex played on its infinite board, with Red and Blue claiming tiles according to the usual rules. The initial position assigns exactly one tile to Red and no tiles to Blue.

**Red's one-tile advantage conjecture.** A game of Infinite Hex with exactly one tile of the board assigned to Red at the initial position, and none to Blue, is a win for Red.

The conjecture concerns whether a single initial tile gives Red a decisive advantage in Infinite Hex, despite the intuition that finite initial advantages might be diluted on an infinite board. The source presents it as an open problem and notes that pairing strategies do not appear sufficient; no resolution is given.
